question: What is the primary goal of decontamination in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To reduce the cost of medical equipment
options.B: To remove or destroy pathogenic microorganisms and ensure item safety
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for hand hygiene
options.D: To speed up patient discharge processes

explanation: Decontamination is specifically designed to remove or destroy pathogens so that items and surfaces are rendered safe for handling, reuse, or disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is decontamination particularly critical for nursing students to master in Nigeria?

options.A: It guarantees a promotion in the hospital hierarchy
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical documentation
options.C: It helps prevent healthcare-associated infections and combats antimicrobial resistance
options.D: It is only required in surgical theatres

explanation: Mastering decontamination helps student nurses prevent HCAIs and minimize the spread of resistant microbial strains in various clinical settings. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following processes must always precede disinfection and sterilization?
explanation: Cleaning is the essential first step that physically removes organic soil and debris, which could otherwise shield microorganisms from chemical or thermal agents. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: What distinguishes sterilization from disinfection?

options.A: Sterilization destroys all forms of microbial life including bacterial spores, whereas disinfection destroys most pathogens but not necessarily spores.
options.B: Disinfection is used only for surgical instruments inside an autoclave.
options.C: Sterilization is performed using ordinary soap and water.
options.D: Disinfection guarantees zero microbial presence on any surface.

explanation: Sterilization achieves complete eradication of all viable microorganisms including resistant endospores, while disinfection reduces pathogenic loads short of complete spore elimination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which category of the Spaulding classification applies to items that enter sterile body tissues or the vascular system?
explanation: Critical items enter sterile body spaces or blood vessels and carry a high infection risk, requiring complete sterilization before use. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: An item such as a blood pressure cuff that touches only intact skin belongs to which Spaulding category?
explanation: Items contacting only intact skin pose minimal risk and are classified as non-critical, typically requiring low-level disinfection or simple cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: To which group of patients should standard precautions be applied?

options.C: All patients regardless of their infection status
options.D: Only patients admitted to the intensive care unit

explanation: Standard precautions are designed for universal application to every patient, acknowledging that any individual may harbor infectious agents. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is considered a core element of standard precautions?

options.A: Isolating all patients in private rooms
options.B: Using personal protective equipment (PPE) based on exposure risk
options.C: Skipping hand hygiene if gloves are worn
options.D: Disinfecting non-critical items with dry heat sterilization

explanation: The appropriate selection and use of PPE according to anticipated exposure is a fundamental component of standard precautions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for keeping used instruments moist before they reach the decontamination room?

options.B: To prevent organic matter and blood from drying out and sticking to the surfaces
options.C: To cool them down after surgery
options.D: To eliminate the need for enzymatic detergents

explanation: Keeping items moist prevents blood and soil from drying, which makes subsequent cleaning much easier and more effective. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the recommended approach for decontaminating routine environmental surfaces?

options.A: Cleaning with detergent followed by disinfectant application
options.B: Immersing the entire surface in an autoclave
options.D: Applying high-level chemical sterilants to floors

explanation: Environmental surfaces are routinely decontaminated using a two-step method involving cleaning with detergent followed by disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is pre-cleaning essential before applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Organic matter can neutralize or shield microorganisms from chemical disinfectants.
options.B: Disinfectants work best when surfaces are completely dry and caked with blood.
options.C: Pre-cleaning replaces the need for correct chemical dilution.
options.D: It extends the expiry date of the disinfectant.

explanation: Organic material like blood and body fluids can inactivate disinfectants or shield pathogens, making pre-cleaning mandatory. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: What factor must nurses strictly observe regarding chemical disinfectant use?

options.A: Using maximum concentration regardless of manufacturer instructions
options.B: Ignoring recommended contact times to speed up work
options.C: Following correct dilution and providing adequate wet contact time
options.D: Mixing different chemical disinfectants together to enhance potency

explanation: Following correct dilution guidelines and ensuring adequate wet contact time are vital to achieve the desired level of microbial destruction. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: What type of gloves is most appropriate when performing manual instrument decontamination?
explanation: Heavy-duty utility gloves provide the necessary puncture and chemical resistance required during manual instrument cleaning and decontamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take following an accidental chemical splash to the eyes in the decontamination room?

options.A: Rub the eyes vigorously with a dry towel
options.B: Flush the eyes immediately at an eyewash station and report the incident
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to seek medical attention
options.D: Apply an alcohol-based hand rub to the eyes

explanation: Immediate flushing at an eyewash station dilutes and removes the chemical agent, minimizing tissue damage, followed by formal incident reporting. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: Where should used needles and other sharps be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: In a black general waste polythene bag
options.C: Into a puncture-proof safety box without recapping
options.D: Into a basin of soapy water

explanation: Sharps must be discarded immediately into dedicated puncture-proof safety boxes without recapping to prevent needlestick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)

question: What is the correct initial step when managing a blood or body fluid spillage on the floor?

options.A: Ignore it until the cleaning staff arrive at the end of the shift
options.B: Put on appropriate PPE and restrict access to the spill area
options.C: Sweep the wet fluid away using a dry broom
options.D: Pour boiling water over the spill without cleaning

explanation: Donning PPE and restricting access ensures personal safety and prevents the spread of contamination before cleaning and disinfection begin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)
